agree.reason: The speaker concedes the C-to-D drop as a fellow Alder Road driver, frames it as a trade against 64 homes, and gives traffic-focused commissioners a way to vote yes with a condition, though opposed neighbours may still not be moved.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the traffic harm is stated plainly; 'about one in six' (64/412 ≈ 1 in 6.4) is fair, but 'Not anyone's backyard' and '64 households stop waiting' are a little stronger than the facts guarantee.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the one-in-six share of the waiting list and the parking surplus of eight, but leaves out other figures it could have drawn, such as what share of the 2,100-home shortfall this meets or how the 310 daily trips spread across the day.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately: the lot stays empty six days a week and 412 households keep waiting, with the three-year average wait already given, though it doesn't spell out how the backlog compounds over time.

qualification.reason: The suggested approval condition, a signal-timing review at Alder and 4th, is sensible but has no date, threshold or consequence, so the commission can't check whether it worked.

objections.reason: It meets the main traffic objection directly and honestly and pre-empts parking with the 72-space figure, but it doesn't test how serious a rush-hour D actually is.

fit.reason: At roughly 430 words in short spoken sentences with a clear ask at the start and end, it fits a three-minute public comment.
